summary: Min Ling Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Min Thu Wun (1909–2004) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Rangoon under Pe Maung Tin (~1927–1935) and at the University of Oxford (~1936–1939).
Minakshi Banerjee works in Indology, having completed her doctorate under Debarchana Sarkar. As of 2026, she holds the James Prinsep Research Fellowship at The Asiatic Society.
Mineo Hashimoto (1924–1984) worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1944–1948) and held a post at Kobe University from around 1953 to 1984.

Ming Mei works in Buddhist studies. She earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan, and studied at SOAS University of London under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.

Ming-Wood Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Hong Kong and earned his PhD at UCLA under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en, later serving as professor at the University of Hong Kong (~1980–2008).
Mingyu Fu works in Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Huifeng Shi (attested 2013).

Minori Nishimura (b. 1947) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD at Taisho University under Shunkyo Katsumata and Seiren Matsunami, later serving as associate professor there, researcher at Sanko Cultural Institute, and with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Minoru Hara (1930–2021) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo, Harvard, and Cambridge. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1975–1991), president of ICABS (1996–2006), and director of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~2000–2009).

Minoru Kiyota (1923–2013) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo under Reimon Yuki, Shinsho Hanayama, Hajime Nakamura, and Akira Hirakawa. He was a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1963–1993).

Minton Warren (1850–1907) was a linguist educated at Tufts, Yale (under William Dwight Whitney), Leipzig, Bonn, and Strasbourg. He held posts at Johns Hopkins University (1879–1899), the American Academy in Rome (1896–1899), and Harvard University (1899).
Minyak Kunzang Sonam studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

id: P:Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo
summary: Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Mipam Chökyi Jampa studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Mipam Gyatso studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi, teacher Robert A. F. Thurman, and postdoctoral mentor Bratindra Nath Mukherjee.

Mircea Eliade (1907–1986) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Bucharest and Calcutta under Surendranath Dasgupta, he taught at Bucharest, EPHE, and the Sorbonne, and became professor at the University of Chicago in 1957.

Mireille Helffer (1928–2023) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and other fields. She served as Chargé de Recherche at CNRS (~1967–1989) and was affiliated with Paris Nanterre University (attested 1985).
Mirella Lingorska works in Indology and linguistics. She has held posts as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich and at the University of Tübingen, both attested in 2026.

Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD from the University of Calgary under John A. Baker, and held affiliations with the University of Western Australia and UNSW.
